sections.h2: What should a seller know about San Antonio itself?
sections.html:
San Antonio sits at the head of the San Antonio River in Bexar County, and its reach across the region is shaped by three interstates and two loops.

The Texas State Historical Association points to Interstate 10 running east and west, Interstates 35 and 37 running north and south, plus Loop 410, State Loop 1604, the international airport and daily Amtrak service. The city has a roughly 300-year history that began with a presidio, a town and five Franciscan missions along the river, and it was the largest city in Texas through the second half of the nineteenth century. Nicknames such as Alamo City, River City and Military City, U.S.A. reflect that story. For a seller, the practical point is size: neighborhoods, ages of housing and commute patterns vary widely from one side of the loops to the other.

  • Compare recent sales within a mile or two of your house, not citywide numbers.
  • Ask a local agent or appraiser which side of Loop 410 or 1604 your house falls on.
  • Check flood and drainage maps if your house sits near the river or a creek.

sections.h2: Which selling route suits a San Antonio house best?
sections.html:
Listing with an agent suits a house in good condition and a seller with time, while a cash sale suits a house that needs work or a seller on a deadline.

In a city this large, expect a wide spread of buyers and prices. A traditional sale usually brings the highest number but adds showings, inspections and lender conditions. Selling by owner removes the agent commission and leaves you with marketing, negotiation and paperwork. A cash buyer purchases as-is and can set a closing date you pick, at a price that reflects repair and resale costs. Ask for each buyer's offer in writing and compare the net to you after closing costs.

  • List if the house is clean, updated and your date is flexible.
  • Take cash if you face a lien, a vacant inherited house or a tenant problem.
  • Never sign before reading who pays title, recording and any repair credits.

sections.h2: Who appraises and bills property tax in San Antonio?
sections.html:
The Bexar Central Appraisal District sets the value, and the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector takes payment, so you deal with two offices.

The appraisal district's site says plainly that it does not accept tax payments and sends payment questions to the tax assessor-collector. Its 2026 notice banner explains that notices went to new owners and to owners whose market value rose by $1,000 or more, and that you do not need a notice to submit a protest. Statewide, Texas values property as of January 1, tax bills go out around October 1 and payment is due by January 31. The city and other units that tax your lot, such as school districts, each set their own rate.

sections.h2: Which dates should a San Antonio owner keep in mind?
sections.html:
Mark January 1, May 15, October 1 and January 31, and note the split payment dates if you want to pay in halves.

Texas property tax schedule as it applies to Bexar County owners (Texas Comptroller)
DateWhat it means
January 1Valuation date and lien date
April 30Common exemption filing cutoff
May 15Usual protest deadline
July 20Review board approves appraisal records
September 29Deadline for most units to adopt rates
February 1Delinquency begins on unpaid taxes

The full list is on the Comptroller calendar.

sections.h2: How do I handle back taxes before selling in San Antonio?
sections.html:
Ask the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector for the amount due, then plan to pay it at or before closing, because the lien stays with the property.

Penalty and interest start at six and one percent on February 1, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1 with interest still growing. If the unit uses a collection attorney, up to 20 percent more can be added. A homestead owner may ask for an installment plan, and some collectors stretch it to 36 months. If suit follows, a tax sale may be held, and the former owner has two years to claim any excess proceeds.

  • Pay at least the undisputed amount if you are appealing a value.
  • Keep receipts for each payment.
  • Tell the closer about any plan so it is handled correctly.

sections.h2: What homestead relief could a San Antonio owner claim?
sections.html:
Owners can claim the residence homestead exemption, with added relief for age, disability or veteran status.

School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead, and owners 65 or older or disabled get an added $60,000. Any unit may adopt a local exemption of up to 20 percent of value, with a minimum of $5,000. The homestead's appraised value is capped at a 10 percent yearly increase. Disabled veterans can receive from $5,000 up to $12,000 depending on rating, and a 100 percent rating can earn a full exemption on a homestead. Heirs who are not on a recorded deed need an affidavit, a death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim one.

sections.h2: What do squatters and holdover occupants mean for a San Antonio sale?
sections.html:
An occupant who stays after being told to leave may be removed through a justice court eviction or, in limited cases, a sheriff or constable request under Property Code chapter 24B.

The chapter 24B route applies when the occupant refused to leave, the property was not open to the public when they entered, no lawsuit is pending between you and the occupant, and the person is not a family member or a current or former tenant. A wrongful removal can lead to a lawsuit against the owner. For tenants, the usual notice is at least three days, and a writ of possession follows only after judgment and a wait of six days.

sections.h2: How is a San Antonio deed recorded?
sections.html:
The Bexar County Clerk records deeds for property in the county, and a deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer.

The state clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 per added page, with additional records fees. Title companies usually file after closing.

faqs.q: Which office collects San Antonio property tax?
faqs.a: The Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector. The Bexar Central Appraisal District says it does not accept payments.

faqs.q: Do I need a notice to protest my value in San Antonio?
faqs.a: No. The Bexar Central Appraisal District says you do not need a notice to submit a protest. Most protests are due May 15 or 30 days after notice delivery if later.

faqs.q: What homestead exemption do school districts give?
faqs.a: They must exempt $140,000 of the home's value, plus an added $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled.

faqs.q: What happens to the lien when a San Antonio house sells?
faqs.a: It stays with the property, so unpaid tax is cleared from sale proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: When does Texas foreclosure sale happen near San Antonio?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of a month between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m., after a notice of sale at least 21 days earlier.
